title: The constructed Int is initial among Z-structures
statement: A `Z-structure` is a carrier R with a point e and two endomorphisms up, down that are mutually inverse (down(up x) = x and up(down x) = x for every x) -- a pointed set with an automorphism, and NOTHING else: no generation, no aperiodicity, no order. Under only those two inverse laws, there is a map f : Int -> R with f(0) = e, f(t+1) = up(f(t)) and f(t-1) = down(f(t)), and it is the UNIQUE such map: any g : Int -> R satisfying the same three equations agrees with f at every point. This is the universal property of Int as the initial object in the category of Z-structures. It is weaker than `Int.Characterization.categorical` (F:int-characterization-categorical), which additionally assumes the target is GENERATED by e under +-1 and APERIODIC at e, and concludes the comparison map is a bijection. The two extra hypotheses are what rule out Z/n (fails aperiodicity) and Z sqcup Z (fails generation) as counter-models to categoricity; neither is needed for mere initiality, because a Z-structure's defining axioms are exactly the two inverse laws, not those two further ones. Uniqueness is stated pointwise (`g t = f t`), not as function equality -- there is no funext in this kernel (ADR-1595) to promote the pointwise claim to one.

formal.statement: theorem Int.Characterization.initial.{u} : ((x0 : Sort (u)) -> ((x1 : x0) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : x0) -> x0)) -> ((x3 : ((x3 : x0) -> x0)) -> ((x4 : ((x4 : x0) -> Eq.{u} x0 (x3 (x2 x4)) x4)) -> ((x5 : ((x5 : x0) -> Eq.{u} x0 (x2 (x3 x5)) x5)) -> And (And (Eq.{u} x0 (Int.Characterization.iter.{u} x0 x1 x2 x3 Int.zero) x1) (And (((x6 : Int) -> Eq.{u} x0 (Int.Characterization.iter.{u} x0 x1 x2 x3 (Int.add x6 Int.one)) (x2 (Int.Characterization.iter.{u} x0 x1 x2 x3 x6)))) (((x6 : Int) -> Eq.{u} x0 (Int.Characterization.iter.{u} x0 x1 x2 x3 (Int.add x6 (Int.neg Int.one))) (x3 (Int.Characterization.iter.{u} x0 x1 x2 x3 x6)))))) (((x6 : ((x6 : Int) -> x0)) -> ((x7 : And (Eq.{u} x0 (x6 Int.zero) x1) (And (((x7 : Int) -> Eq.{u} x0 (x6 (Int.add x7 Int.one)) (x2 (x6 x7)))) (((x7 : Int) -> Eq.{u} x0 (x6 (Int.add x7 (Int.neg Int.one))) (x3 (x6 x7)))))) -> ((x8 : Int) -> Eq.{u} x0 (x6 x8) (Int.Characterization.iter.{u} x0 x1 x2 x3 x8)))))))))))

evidence.supports: Int admits a structure-preserving map out of it into any Z-structure, and that map is the unique one -- with an empty axiom footprint.

evidence.supports: The theorem is not vacuous: instantiated at (Int, 0, (+1), (-1)) with the two inverse-law hypotheses discharged by the ring laws (add_assoc, add_zero, add_neg, add_comm) -- the same construction categorical_at_int uses for the stronger theorem -- and pushed back through the trusted gate with an empty footprint.
evidence.notes: A theorem whose hypothesis list nothing satisfies is axiom-free and worthless; this closes that for the two inverse laws exactly as categorical_at_int closes it for the full four-hypothesis list of categoricity.

evidence.supports: Dropping the packaged uniqueness clause's `g 0 = e` hypothesis (Weakening::IntInitialDropUniqueZero) while the proof still supplies the real equation makes the kernel REFUSE Int.Characterization.initial, at the declaration itself.

provenance.source: Named and proved from the already-admitted Int.Characterization.iter_zero, iter_succ, iter_pred and rec_unique -- see docs/research/09-decisions/adr-1610-name-the-universal-properties.md for why this is a separate, weaker theorem than Int.Characterization.categorical (F:int-characterization-categorical) rather than a restatement of it.

notes: WHY THIS FACT EXISTS. `Int.Characterization.categorical` (F:int-characterization-categorical) already exists and is strictly stronger, but its four-hypothesis list conflates two different things: the two axioms that make (R, e, up, down) a Z-structure at all (the inverse laws), and the two further axioms that pin it to be isomorphic to Int specifically (generation, aperiodicity) rather than to Z/n or Z sqcup Z. This fact isolates the first pair and names the result: mere initiality, unconditional on generation or aperiodicity. NOT A NEW PROOF: iter's own computation rules and Int.Characterization.rec_unique are applied directly, so a drift in any of the four underlying statements this depends on would make Int.Characterization.initial FAIL TO TYPE-CHECK. See docs/research/08-planning/universal-property-template.md for the four-part template this fact and F:nat-peano-initial both follow.
